title: Batched Inference Slot Pricing — personal scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick mental model for a slot-based pricing alternative to pure per-token billing. Goal is a small set of offering sketches we can sanity-check with product and infra: cheap to explain, maps to latency SLOs and batching gains, gives predictable revenue for Dedicated customers, and is easy to instrument in Console.

High level idea (TL;DR): sell discrete "inference slots" (time-windowed reservation of capacity) rather than tokens. Each slot corresponds to a small GPU-time budget plus a KV/cache residency budget. Customers consume slots per request depending on concurrency and batchability; tokens still affect slot consumption via sequence-length multiplier. Slots simplify predictability: easier to map to GPU-hours and to guarantee latency SLOs.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- 1x A100-80GB equivalent (or dedicated vfslot) amortized cost to us: $3.60/hour (hosted blended) — replace with real infra numbers later.
- Effective usable throughput depends on batching; for average convo workload we can get 6x throughput with continuous batching vs naive single-request serving.
- Typical average sequence length: 200 input tokens + 100 generated tokens for product workloads (search/assist use cases vary).
- Target latency SLO for slot product: p95 <= 350ms. This implies small batching windows (10–40ms) and warm KV cache.

Define a slot:
- Slot duration: 1 second of GPU availability (logical), i.e., entitlement to be scheduled on a GPU for 1s within a small SLA window.
- Base slot volume: number of tokens one slot can produce depends on concurrency and batching. Base assumption for math here: 1 slot -> 400 tokens output equivalents when well-batched (amortized).
- Sequence-length multiplier: long contexts consume more KV and decoder time; define multiplier = (input_tokens + output_tokens) / 400, so slot consumption = ceil(multiplier * base_slots).
- Cold penalty: first request after >5min idle uses 2x slots (KV warm-up, cache miss).

Arithmetic (sketch):
- Cost to us: $3.60/hour -> per-second = $0.001 per second. If we map 1 slot = 1 second of GPU availability, cost-per-slot = $0.001. But this is low-level; we need overheads (ops, infra, margin).
- Add 3x multiplier for ops + margins -> cost-basis per slot = $0.003.
- If 1 slot => 400 tokens, cost-per-1k-tokens = (0.003 / 400) * 1000 = $0.0075. Compare to current hosted per-token target (example) $0.03/1k for large models -> slot model is cheaper on well-batched workloads.

Revenue framing (examples):
- Nano pack: 100 slots / month -> pays for bursty demo apps. 100 * cost_basis of $0.003 = $0.30 cost to us per month; price at $5/mo -> margin and UX value for low-usage customers.
- Developer pack: 5k slots / month -> price $150/mo -> implies $0.03/slot retail (example).
- Dedicated reserved: buy reserved pool of 2000 concurrent slots (effective parallelism) with monthly commit, priced to reflect reserved discount vs hosted. This maps more cleanly to Dedicated capacity and predictable throughput.

Behavioral mechanics (how requests consume slots):
- Single request arrives -> scheduler tries to batch it for up to 25ms to improve utilization. If batched with n requests, assigned slot consumption = base_slots/n (rounded up) but with per-request multipliers for sequence length. Alternative: assign fractional slot credit and settle monthly. Simpler: always charge integer slots after per-request multiplier and then aggregate per-minute.
- Background agents (embedding bulk jobs) should be mapped to longer-slot variants (e.g., 10s slot) with steep discount.

Pros / cons (brain dump):
Pros:
- Easier to map to Dedicated SKU: slots ~ reserved concurrency.
- Gives customers a clearer SLO-backed product: X slots = Y guaranteed throughput at p95 latency.
- Encourages batching, cache-friendly patterns (good for our unit economics).
- Lower friction for billing predictability on bursty interactive apps.
Cons / risks:
- Cognitive load: customers understand tokens, not slots. Need UX/SDK helpers showing tokens->slots conversion.
- Granularity problems: rounding integer slots may annoy low-volume users. Need fractional accounting or minute-level pooling.
- Edge cases: streaming with long tails, tool-calling (external I/O) can blow slot economics.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should slots be time-based (1s) or work-based (GPU cycles / FLOP proxies)? Time-based easiest to explain; work-based ties to model size and sequence length.
- How to handle model heterogeneity? Larger models should consume more slots per second (or require higher-cost slot class). Need multiple slot classes (small/medium/large) with clear conversions.
- Backfill accounting for batched fairness: do we charge the batch owner full slots, or distribute slots across callers? Prefer per-request fractional credits and round in daily bill.
- UX: show estimated slots for example API call in Console; provide estimator in SDK that computes projected monthly spend given qps/avg tokens/desired p95.
- Integration with credits/free-tier: grant X slots as starter credits. Map existing credits to equivalent slots for migration.

Quick scenario sanity-check (very rough):
- Simple chat app: 50 concurrent users, avg 1.5 requests/minute each, avg tokens 300 per request -> QPS = 1.25, monthly requests ~ 3.24M. If 1 slot covers 400 tokens -> slot consumption ~ (300/400)*3.24M = 2.43M slots/month. At example price $0.03/slot retail -> $72.9k/mo (obviously pricing tuned)—this highlights that slot unit price must be tiny or slots represent larger token bundles. Alternatively, price per-slot $0.0003 (then revenue more reasonable). Need to calibrate to existing per-token numbers.

Edge case notes:
- Embeddings: extremely high token-to-cost ratio; create separate slot class or keep per-embedding pricing.
- Batch CPU-only ops: disallow slot discounts if no GPU used.

Next steps if we want to push this further:
- Pull actual blended infra costs from infra-finance for A100/P4 clusters.
- Simulate 3 workload traces (chat/assistant, docs-processing, classification) to compute effective tokens/slot at different batching windows (0ms, 10ms, 50ms).
- Prototype estimator in Console/SDK that given qps, avg token lengths, desired p95 returns suggested monthly slot pack and a comparison to token-based bill.
- Mock up 3 offers: dev/nano, team, and reserved-dedicated mapping.

Notes to self: keep language customer-centered: present slot as "throughput credits" or "fast-response credits" not "GPU seconds". Frame discounted reserved slots as predictable throughput for mission-critical apps.

Random jotters: 
- Could combine with SLO add-on: paying for "priority slots" that get scheduled before best-effort. Good for multi-tenant hosted.
- Avoid too many SKU variants; two slot sizes + reserved/burst add-ons might suffice.

End of scratchpad.

(Scattered TODOs inline; will tidy for product doc if we move forward.)
